sections.html:
Two separate offices handle Lee County's tax side. For value, exemptions and the mailing address on file, dial the appraiser at 239-533-6100. For anything about paying, dial the collector at 239-533-6000.

Sellers run into this at closing. Value and exemption changes are off the table at the collector's counter, and the appraiser takes no money. Roads, fire, water and sewer assessments belong to whichever authority levied them, and its contact information sits on the bill.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial payment plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and petitions in value disputes.

Payment season starts November 1 and ends March 31 of the next calendar year. Whatever is still owed on April 1 is delinquent.

Florida's early-pay scale gives 4 percent in November, then one point less each month until February; March earns nothing. If the notice still names a lender after you paid the loan off, the November discount is not blocked, the collector says.

One calendar covers every city here, Cape Coral through Sanibel. Owners can pay six ways: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax calls for more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so arrange certified money ahead of any closing.

sections.h2: Payment plans from the Lee County Tax Collector
sections.html:
Owners can choose quarterly installments, partial payments or homestead deferral, and the installment application is the first to close.

Lee County payment plans at a glance
PlanApplyMain rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

The first installment earns 6 percent, the second 4.5 percent, the third 3 percent and the last nothing. A first payment not made by July 31 ends enrollment. Partial payments apply to the live tax year only and never to delinquent tax, and installment enrollees cannot add them.

A mid-year sale leaves the plan running, since the new owner takes it over through year end. Let the closing agent know early.

The first $25,000 of assessed value is exempt from every levy under homestead. The appraiser prints a second layer of up to $26,411 for 2026, which reaches non-school levies only and sits on value above $50,000.

File Form DR-501 by March 1. Choices: online at leepa.org, email to exemptions@leepa.org, mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or hand delivery at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, during weekday business hours. The office completes processing by July 1. Save Our Homes, which limits annual assessment increases, starts one year after the grant.

Senior exemptions for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over differ by taxing body:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veteran owners, disabled first responders, surviving spouses and deployed service members, plus $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew every January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

sections.h2: What happens to homestead when you sell?
sections.html:
The exemption does not transfer. The buyer files a new application, and yours ends at the start of the next year.

If a TRIM notice lists homestead in the purchase year, it is showing the seller's benefit, and that will be taken off. Long-term renting can end the exemption, as can moving title into certain trusts or LLCs. The office asks to be told about every ownership change.

Buying again in Florida means a new homestead application at the new address, along with a portability claim for the Save Our Homes benefit. The state allows three years, counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead ended, and the portability form is DR-501T, due March 1.

The appraiser mails TRIM in mid-August as a preview. The real charge arrives from the collector, usually in November, and only the bill lists non-ad valorem items such as garbage, fire or water.

On the notice you will see market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. To contest a value, petition the Value Adjustment Board inside 25 days of the notice date; a denied exemption has its own 30 days from the denial letter. Save both documents for any buyer curious about carrying costs.

Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027, the collector's FAQ answers, so the 2026 bill is unaffected. Millage depends on your address, across school, city and district levies, so rely on your parcel lookup and notice, not a countywide average.

sections.h2: Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?
sections.html:
On the settlement statement, the closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties. The bill, though, goes to the owner of record at the time the roll reaches the collector, which means a past owner can still get one in the mail.

Forward it to the new owner or the closing agent. Transfers are recorded by the clerk and relayed to the appraiser afterward, so delays happen. Any unpaid tax turns up in the title search and is cleared from seller funds.

The stamp tax on a Lee County deed is the usual Florida rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Miami-Dade differs). Both parties are answerable, and payment goes to the clerk when the deed is recorded.

About 875,607 people live in this Gulf Coast county, 15.1 percent more than in 2020. The county has 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent occupied by their owners, and a median home value of $362,200 for 2020 to 2024. With 29.2 percent of residents at 65 or older, the senior exemptions above matter in many sales.

Incorporated areas are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach; everything else is unincorporated and handled by the same two offices.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell: a short checklist
sections.html:
1. Search your parcel on the appraiser's site and confirm the owner name and mailing address.
  2. Get a current balance from the collector, including word on any delinquent year.
  3. On installments? Collect a record of what you have paid and give it to the closing agent.
  4. Set aside the TRIM notice and last tax bill in case buyers ask about costs.
  5. Pick the location of your next homestead early, so the portability filing can be planned.

A cash buyer skips lender underwriting, yet the title search still shows unpaid tax, so the same papers apply.

faqs.q: Do the Lee County tax dates change each year?
faqs.a: No. The calendar repeats: open November 1, due March 31, delinquent April 1, with a discount that falls from 4 percent to 1 percent between November and February.

faqs.q: Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?
faqs.a: No. Applications run November 1 to April 30. After that, only partial payments remain, open through March 31.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?
faqs.a: No. The buyer files a new application, and a TRIM notice that lists homestead after a purchase is still showing the seller's old benefit.

faqs.q: Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Start with the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition uses a DR-486 form, filed with the clerk inside 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

faqs.q: What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?
faqs.a: It is paid from your proceeds at closing, with any added charges. Late tax cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck, so ask the collector what funds it accepts.
